`memory.store.complete` | Store confirmed |\n| `memory.recall.request` | Recall request |\n| `memory.recall.complete` | Recall results |\n| `memory.context.assembled` | Context window ready |\n\n### 3.8 Response Events (source: kernel, executor)\n\n| Type | Description |\n|------|-------------|\n| `response.ok` | Request completed successfully |\n| `response.error` | Request completed with error |\n| `response.timeout` | Request timed out |\n| `response.rejected` | Request rejected (no capability) |\n\n### 3.9 System Events (source: kernel, boot)\n\n| Type | Description |\n|------|-------------|\n| `system.boot` | Kernel started |\n| `system.shutdown` | Kernel stopping |\n| `system.error` | Unhandled system error |\n| `system.telemetry` | Periodic metrics |\n\n---\n\n## 4. Subject Naming (NATS)\n\n### 4.1 Pattern\n\n```\nethan.<domain>.<source>.<action>\n```\n\n| Segment | Values | Example |\n|---------|--------|---------|\n| `domain` | `interface`, `kernel`, `registry`, `planner`, `executor`, `module`, `memory`, `response`, `system`, `capability` | `planner` |\n| `source` | Component name | `planner` |\n| `action` | Event type action | `plan.created` |\n\n### 4.2 Subject Table\n\n| Subject | Publisher | Subscribers |\n|---------|-----------|-------------|\n| `ethan.interface.cli` | CLI | Kernel |\n| `ethan.interface.api` | API gateway | Kernel |\n| `ethan.kernel.request.created` | Kernel | Planner |\n| `ethan.registry.capability.registered` | Module | Registry |\n| `ethan.registry.updated` | Registry | All |\n| `ethan.planner.plan.created` | Planner | Executor |\n| `ethan.planner.plan.failed` | Planner | Kernel |\n| `ethan.executor.task.assigned` | Executor | Module |\n| `ethan.executor.task.completed` | Module | Executor |\n| `ethan.executor.task.failed` | Module | Executor |\n| `ethan.capability.<name>` | Executor | Module |\n| `ethan.capability.<name>.completed` | Module | Executor |\n| `ethan.memory.store.request` | Any | Memory |\n| `ethan.memory.recall.complete` | Memory | Requestor |\n| `ethan.response.<correlation_id>` | Kernel | Interface |\n| `ethan.ingest.error` | Ingest | Telemetry |\n| `ethan.system.error` | Kernel | Telemetry |\n\n### 4.3 Wildcard Patterns\n\n| Pattern | Matches |\n|---------|---------|\n| `ethan.interface.>` | All interface events |\n| `ethan.planner.*` | All planner events |\n| `ethan.capability.*` | All capability invocations |\n| `ethan.capability.*.completed` | All capability results |\n| `ethan.>` | All system events |\n\n---\n\n## 5. Pub/Sub Model\n\n### 5.1 Go Interface\n\n```go\ntype EventBus interface {\n    Connect(addr string) error\n    Publish(subject string, data []byte)\n    Subscribe(pattern string, handler func([]byte)) (int, error)\n    Close()\n}\n```\n\n### 5.2 Python Interface\n\n```python\nclass EventBus(ABC):\n    async def connect(self, servers: str) -> None: ...\n    async def publish(self, topic: str, event: Event) -> None: ...\n    async def subscribe(self, topic: str, handler, queue: str = None) -> Subscription: ...\n    async def request(self, topic: str, event: Event, timeout: float) -> Optional[Event]: ...\n    async def close(self) -> None: ...\n```\n\n### 5.3 Delivery Guarantees\n\n| Guarantee | Implementation |\n|-----------|---------------|\n| At-least-once | NATS JetStream durable subscriptions |\n| Ordered per subject | Same subject → same order |\n| No message loss | JetStream persistence + PostgreSQL backup |\n| Queue groups | Load-balanced between subscribers of same group |\n\n### 5.4 Patterns\n\n| Pattern | Description | Use Case |\n|---------|-------------|----------|\n| **Pub/Sub** | One publisher, many subscribers | Interface events, system broadcasts |\n| **Queue Groups** | One publisher, one consumer from group | Task assignment (one module handles) |\n| **Request/Reply** | Publish and wait for response | Capability query, status check |\n\n---\n\n## 6. Event Lifecycle\n\n```\n1. Source creates Event\n2. Source publishes to NATS subject\n3. NATS delivers to all matching subscribers\n4. Each subscriber deserializes Event\n5. Subscriber processes Event (async)\n6. Subscriber may publish result Event\n7. Result event delivered to its subscribers\n```\n\n**Example flow**:\n```\nCLI publishes: ethan.interface.cli\n  │\n  ▼\nKernel receives, creates Request\n  │\n  ▼\nPlanner receives, creates Plan\n  │\n  ▼\nExecutor receives, assigns task → ethan.capability.docker.build\n  │\n  ▼\nDocker module receives, executes, publishes result\n  │\n  ▼\nExecutor receives result, publishes ethan.response.<correlation_id>\n```\n\n---\n\n## 7. Error Handling\n\n| Failure | Behavior |\n|---------|----------|\n| Publish fails | Logged, no retry (caller responsible) |\n| Subscribe fails | Logged, system may not start |\n| Handler panics | Caught and logged, subscription stays active |\n| Unknown event type | Logged, event not routed |\n| Malformed event | Logged, event not routed |\n\n---\n\n## 8. Existing Implementations\n\n| Implementation | Language | File | Status |\n|---------------|----------|------|--------|\n| Abstract interface | Python | `kernel/bus/interface.py` | Stable |\n| NATS JetStream impl | Python | `kernel/bus/nats_bus.py` | Stable |\n| In-memory bus | Go | `kernel/bus/bus.go` | Development |\n| Event type | Go | `kernel/types/event.go` | Development |\n\n---\n\n## Appendix A: Example Event Sequence\n\n```\nStep 1: User types \"ethan status\"\n─────────────────────────────────\nPublisher: CLI\nSubject:   ethan.interface.cli\nEvent:\n  id: 20260623150500.000000001\n  type: interface.command\n  source: cli\n  payload: {\"cmd\": \"ethan status\"}\n\nStep 2: Kernel receives, validates, creates request\n─────────────────────────────────\nSubject:   ethan.kernel.request.created\nEvent:\n  type: kernel.request.created\n  source: kernel\n  payload: {\"intent\": \"status\", \"request_id\": \"...\"}\n\nStep 3: Planner creates execution plan\n─────────────────────────────────\nSubject:   ethan.planner.plan.created\nEvent:\n  type: planner.plan.created\n  source: planner\n  payload: {\"plan_id\": \"...\", \"tasks\": [...]}\n\nStep 4: Executor publishes response\n─────────────────────────────────\nSubject:   ethan.response.20260623150500.000000001\nEvent:\n  type: response.ok\n  source: executor\n  payload: {\"status\": \"online\", \"mode\": \"idle\", \"goal\": \"none\"}\n```","operationIsLocatedInWorkspace":true,"startLineNumbers":[]}

{"tool":"newFileCreated","path":"EVENT_LIFECYCLE.md","content":"# ETHAN Event Lifecycle Specification\n\n## 1. Lifecycle Overview\n\nEvery event in the system follows exactly 5 steps:\n\n```\n[1] EMIT ──► [2] INTERCEPT ──► [3] ROUTE ──► [4] PROCESS ──► [5] RESPOND\n```\n\nEach step is a discrete phase with defined input, output, and tracing boundaries.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Step Details\n\n### 2.1 EMIT\n\n**Purpose**: Create and publish an event onto the bus.\n\n**Trigger**: Any component generates an event (interface input, module output, timer expiry).\n\n**Rules**:\n- Event must have a unique `id` (UUID or timestamp+nano)\n- Event must have a valid `type` (from `EventType` registry)\n- Event must have a `source` identifying the emitter\n- Event must have a `timestamp` (ISO 8601 UTC)\n- Payload and context are optional but recommended\n\n**Tracing**:\n- Generate `correlation_id` if not inherited\n- Generate `span_id` for this emit step\n- Record `emit_timestamp`\n\n**Pseudocode**:\n```\nfunction emit(source, type, payload):\n    event = {\n        id: generate_id(),\n        type: type,\n        source: source,\n        timestamp: now(),\n        payload: payload,\n        context: {\n            correlation_id: payload.context.correlation_id ?? generate_id(),\n            span_id: generate_id(),\n            parent_span_id: payload.context.span_id ?? nil\n        }\n    }\n    bus.publish(event)\n    return event.id\n```\n\n---\n\n### 2.2 INTERCEPT\n\n**Purpose**: Validate and enrich the event before routing.\n\n**Trigger**: Event arrives at the kernel (via NATS subscriber).\n\n**Steps**:\n1. Deserialize JSON → Event struct\n2. Validate required fields (`id`, `type`, `source`, `timestamp`)\n3. Reject invalid events → emit `ingest.error`\n4. Enrich context if missing (add `ingest_timestamp`)\n5. Pass to Router\n\n**Validation rules**:\n| Check | Failure action |\n|-------|---------------|\n| Missing `id` | Auto-generate, log warning |\n| Missing `type` | Emit `ingest.error`, drop event |\n| Missing `source` | Emit `ingest.error`, drop event |\n| Malformed JSON | Emit `ingest.error`, drop event |\n| Unknown event type | Log warning, route anyway |\n\n**Tracing**:\n- Record `ingest_timestamp`\n- Record `intercept_latency`\n- Attach `kernel_span_id`\n\n**Pseudocode**:\n```\nfunction intercept(event):\n    if !validate(event):\n        emit(\"ingest\", \"ingest.error\", {reason: \"invalid\", event_id: event.id})\n        return nil\n    \n    event.context.ingest_timestamp = now()\n    event.context.kernel_span_id = generate_id()\n    return event\n```\n\n---\n\n### 2.3 ROUTE\n\n**Purpose**: Determine which component(s) should receive the event.\n\n**Trigger**: Event passes interception.\n\n**Algorithm**:\n1. Match event `type` against routing table\n2. Resolve target component (planner, executor, module, etc.)\n3. If capability-based: query registry for target module\n4. If queue group: select one subscriber\n5. If broadcast: deliver to all matching subscribers\n\n**Routing table**:\n| Event Type | Target | Pattern |\n|-----------|--------|---------|\n| `interface.command` | Kernel | Broadcast |\n| `kernel.request.created` | Planner | Queue (one instance) |\n| `planner.plan.created` | Executor | Queue (one instance) |\n| `executor.task.assigned` | Module | Queue (one per capability) |\n| `module.capability.result` | Executor | Direct (by correlation_id) |\n| `response.*` | Interface | Direct (by correlation_id) |\n| `registry.capability.registered` | Registry | Queue |\n| `system.*` | All | Broadcast |\n\n**Tracing**:\n- Record `route_target`\n- Record `route_latency`\n- Attach `routing_span_id`\n\n**Pseudocode**:\n```\nfunction route(event):\n    target = routing_table.match(event.type)\n    if target == nil:\n        log(\"unroutable event:\", event.type)\n        return\n\n    event.context.route_target = target.name\n    event.context.route_timestamp = now()\n    event.context.routing_span_id = generate_id()\n    \n    forward(event, target)\n```\n\n---\n\n### 2.4 PROCESS\n\n**Purpose**: Execute the component's business logic.\n\n**Trigger**: Routed event arrives at the target component.\n\n**Steps**:\n1. Component receives event\n2. Component executes its logic (request decomposition, task execution, etc.)\n3. Component may emit sub-events during processing\n4. Component produces a result\n\n**Processing types**:\n| Component | Input Event | Processing | Output Events |\n|-----------|-------------|------------|---------------|\n| Planner | `kernel.request.created` | Decompose goal → task DAG | `planner.plan.created` |\n| Executor | `planner.plan.created` | Assign tasks, track results | `executor.task.assigned`, `executor.plan.done` |\n| Memory | `memory.*.request` | Store/recall/context | `memory.*.complete` |\n| Registry | `registry.capability.registered` | Validate, store, broadcast | `registry.updated` |\n| Response | `executor.plan.done` | Build response | `response.ok` |\n\n**Tracing**:\n- Record `process_start_timestamp`\n- Record `process_end_timestamp`\n- Record `process_latency = process_end - process_start`\n- Attach `process_span_id`\n- All sub-events inherit `correlation_id` and set `parent_span_id`\n\n**Pseudocode**:\n```\nfunction process(event, component):\n    event.context.process_start = now()\n    event.context.process_span_id = generate_id()\n    \n    result = component.handle(event)\n    \n    event.context.process_end = now()\n    event.context.process_latency = event.context.process_end - event.context.process_start\n    \n    return result\n```\n\n---\n\n### 2.5 RESPOND\n\n**Purpose**: Return the result to the originating interface or caller.\n\n**Trigger**: Processing completes.\n\n**Response types**:\n| Type | When |\n|------|------|\n| `response.ok` | Processing succeeded |\n| `response.error` | Processing failed with error |\n| `response.timeout` | Processing exceeded timeout |\n| `response.rejected` | Processing not possible (no capability) |\n\n**Delivery**:\n1. Response is published to `ethan.response.<correlation_id>`\n2. Interface subscribes to `ethan.response.<correlation_id>` (temporary subscription)\n3. If no subscriber exists, response is logged and discarded\n4. If timeout (no response within TTL), interface emits timeout event\n\n**Tracing**:\n- Record `respond_timestamp`\n- Record `total_latency = respond_timestamp - emit_timestamp`\n- Attach `respond_span_id`\n- Write full trace to telemetry store\n\n**Pseudocode**:\n```\nfunction respond(event, result):\n    response = {\n        id: generate_id(),\n        type: \"response.\" + result.status,\n        source: event.context.route_target,\n        timestamp: now(),\n        payload: result.data,\n        context: {\n            correlation_id: event.context.correlation_id,\n            span_id: generate_id(),\n            parent_span_id: event.context.process_span_id,\n            emit_timestamp: event.context.emit_timestamp,\n            ingest_timestamp: event.context.ingest_timestamp,\n            route_timestamp: event.context.route_timestamp,\n            process_start: event.context.process_start,\n            process_end: event.context.process_end,\n            respond_timestamp: now(),\n            total_latency_ms: now() - event.context.emit_timestamp\n        }\n    }\n    bus.publish(\"ethan.response.\" + event.context.correlation_id, response)\n    telemetry.store_trace(response.context)\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. Complete Lifecycle Timeline\n\n```\nEMIT         INTERCEPT      ROUTE         PROCESS       RESPOND\n│            │              │             │             │\n▼            ▼              ▼             ▼             ▼\n┌──────┐    ┌─────────┐   ┌────────┐   ┌────────┐   ┌────────┐\n│ Create │──►│Validate │──►│ Match  │──►│Execute │──►│ Return │\n│ Event │   │Enrich   │   │Forward │   │Result  │   │Result  │\n└──────┘   └─────────┘    └────────┘   └────────┘   └────────┘\n    │            │              │             │            │\n    ▼            ▼              ▼             ▼            ▼\ntrace:       trace:         trace:        trace:        trace:\nemit_ts      ingest_ts      route_ts      process_ts    respond_ts\nspan_id      kernel_span    routing_span  process_span  respond_span\ncorrelation──►──────correlation_id (inherited throughout)────────────►\n```\n\n---\n\n## 4. Tracing Model\n\n### 4.1 Trace Context Fields\n\n| Field | Generated at | Inherited | Description |\n|-------|-------------|-----------|-------------|\n| `correlation_id` | EMIT | yes (never changed) | Root trace ID for the entire request |\n| `span_id` | EMIT | no | Current processing span |\n| `parent_span_id` | — | yes | Span that triggered this processing |\n| `emit_timestamp` | EMIT | yes | When the root event was created |\n| `ingest_timestamp` | INTERCEPT | no | When kernel received the event |\n| `route_target` | ROUTE | no | Component that will process |\n| `process_start` | PROCESS | no | When processing began |\n| `process_end` | PROCESS | no | When processing ended |\n| `process_latency` | PROCESS | no | Duration of processing |\n| `respond_timestamp` | RESPOND | no | When response was sent |\n| `total_latency_ms` | RESPOND | no | End-to-end duration |\n\n### 4.2 Span Relationships\n\n```\ncorrelation_id: \"req-abc-123\"\n  │\n  ├─ span_id: \"emit-001\" (parent: nil)\n  │\n  ├─ span_id: \"intercept-002\" (parent: \"emit-001\")\n  │\n  ├─ span_id: \"route-003\" (parent: \"intercept-002\")\n  │\n  ├─ span_id: \"process-004\" (parent: \"route-003\")\n  │     │\n  │     ├─ span_id: \"sub-emit-005\" (parent: \"process-004\")\n  │     │     │\n  │     │     └─ span_id: \"sub-process-006\" (parent: \"sub-emit-005\")\n  │     │\n  │     └─ span_id: \"sub-emit-007\" (parent: \"process-004\")\n  │\n  └─ span_id: \"respond-008\" (parent: \"process-004\")\n```\n\n### 4.3 Telemetry Record\n\nAfter RESPOND, the full trace is stored:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"correlation_id\": \"req-abc-123\",\n  \"spans\": [\n    {\"id\": \"emit-001\", \"parent\": null, \"component\": \"cli\", \"type\": \"emit\", \"ts\": \"...\"},\n    {\"id\": \"intercept-002\", \"parent\": \"emit-001\", \"component\": \"kernel\", \"type\": \"intercept\", \"ts\": \"...\", \"latency_ms\": 0.2},\n    {\"id\": \"route-003\", \"parent\": \"intercept-002\", \"component\": \"kernel\", \"type\": \"route\", \"ts\": \"...\", \"target\": \"planner\"},\n    {\"id\": \"process-004\", \"parent\": \"route-003\", \"component\": \"planner\", \"type\": \"process\", \"ts\": \"...\", \"latency_ms\": 45.1},\n    {\"id\": \"respond-008\", \"parent\": \"process-004\", \"component\": \"kernel\", \"type\": \"respond\", \"ts\": \"...\", \"total_latency_ms\": 52.3}\n  ],\n  \"total_latency_ms\": 52.3,\n  \"status\": \"ok\"\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. Error Lifecycle\n\nWhen an error occurs at any step:\n\n```\nEMIT ──► INTERCEPT ──► ROUTE ──► PROCESS ──► RESPOND\n                                   │\n                                   ▼\n                                FAILURE\n                                   │\n                                   ▼\n                              response.error\n                                   │\n                                   ▼\n                              RESPOND (error)\n```\n\nErrors are:\n- Logged at the step where they occur\n- Attached to the response as `error` field\n- Counter metrics incremented in telemetry\n- Propagated through the same lifecycle (the error response goes through RESPOND)\n\n---\n\n## 6. Lifecycle in Go (kernel/main.go)\n\n```go\nfunc (s *Service) HandleEvent(ev types.Event) {\n    // 1. INTERCEPT\n    if err := s.ingest.Process(ev); err != nil {\n        return // error event already emitted\n    }\n\n    // 2. EMIT was done by the interface, ROUTE happens via NATS subject match\n\n    // 3. PROCESS (simplified: planner + executor)\n    intent := s.intent.Extract(ev)\n    req := types.NewRequest(ev, intent.Name, []string{intent.Name}, types.RequestContext{\n        CorrelationID:   ev.Context[\"correlation_id\"],\n        Timestamp:       ev.Timestamp.Unix(),\n    })\n    plan, err := s.planner.Decompose(req)\n    if err != nil || plan == nil {\n        // RESPOND with rejection\n        s.builder.Build(req, nil, fmt.Errorf(\"no capability for intent: %s\", intent.Name))\n        return\n    }\n    results := s.executor.Execute(*plan)\n\n    // 4. RESPOND\n    resp := s.builder.Build(req, results, nil)\n    _ = resp\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 7. Lifecycle in Python (api/routers/message.py)\n\n```python\nasync def post_message(request):\n    # 1. EMIT event to NATS\n    event = Event(id=str(uuid4()), type=\"interface.message\", source=\"api\")\n    await nats.publish(\"ethan.interface.api\", event.dict())\n\n    # Kernel handles INTERCEPT → ROUTE → PROCESS → RESPOND\n\n    # 5. Interface observes RESPOND on subscription\n    # (response is delivered asynchronously)\n    return MessageResponse(success=True, event_id=event.id)\n```\n\n---\n\n## Appendix A: Telemetry API\n\nThe tracing system exposes:\n\n| Operation | Description |\n|-----------|-------------|\n| `telemetry.store_trace(trace)` | Persist completed trace |\n| `telemetry.query_trace(correlation_id)` | Retrieve trace by ID |\n| `telemetry.list_traces(filter)` | List traces by time/status/source |\n| `telemetry.metrics()` | Aggregate latency metrics |\n\nEach trace is immutable once stored. No modification after RESPOND.\n\n---\n\n## Appendix B: Lifecycle Constants\n\n```python\nclass LifecyclePhase:\n    EMIT = \"emit\"\n    INTERCEPT = \"intercept\"\n    ROUTE = \"route\"\n    PROCESS = \"process\"\n    RESPOND = \"respond\"\n    ERROR = \"error\"\n\nclass TraceField:\n    CORRELATION_ID = \"correlation_id\"\n    SPAN_ID = \"span_id\"\n    PARENT_SPAN_ID = \"parent_span_id\"\n    EMIT_TS = \"emit_timestamp\"\n    INGEST_TS = \"ingest_timestamp\"\n    ROUTE_TS = \"route_timestamp\"\n    ROUTE_TARGET = \"route_target\"\n    PROCESS_START = \"process_start\"\n    PROCESS_END = \"process_end\"\n    PROCESS_LATENCY = \"process_latency\"\n    RESPOND_TS = \"respond_timestamp\"\n    TOTAL_LATENCY = \"total_latency_ms\"\n    STATUS = \"status\"\n    ERROR = \"error\"\n```","operationIsLocatedInWorkspace":true,"startLineNumbers":[]}

## ✅ ETHAN Event Lifecycle — specification written

**`EVENT_LIFECYCLE.md`** defines the 5-step lifecycle for every event:

| Step | Phase | Responsibility |
|------|-------|---------------|
| **EMIT** | Create + publish | Component generates event with id, type, source, timestamp, payload, context |
| **INTERCEPT** | Validate + enrich | Deserialize, validate fields, reject invalid, add ingest_timestamp, kernel_span_id |
| **ROUTE** | Match + forward | Routing table lookup → target component (queue group, broadcast, or direct) |
| **PROCESS** | Execute | Component executes business logic (planner, executor, module, memory, registry) |
| **RESPOND** | Return result | Publish `response.*` to `ethan.response.<correlation_id>`, store trace |

**Tracing**: Each step generates `span_id` and timestamps. `correlation_id` inherited throughout. After RESPOND, full trace persisted to telemetry store.

**Error lifecycle**: Errors produce `response.error` through same RESPOND phase.

**Code examples**: Go `kernel/main.go` and Python `api/routers/message.py` show the lifecycle in practice.HAS_CHANGES

{"tool":"newFileCreated","path":"ASYNC_EXECUTION.md","content":"# ETHAN Asynchronous Execution Model\n\n## 1. Architecture Overview\n\n```\nInterface ──► Event Bus (NATS)\n                  │\n                  ├─► Queue Group (Task Assignment) ──► Module A\n                  │\n                  ├─► Queue Group (Task Assignment) ──► Module B\n                  │\n                  └─► Parallel Fan-Out (broadcast) ──► Module C\n                                                        Module D\n```\n\nThree execution primitives:\n- **Parallel** — tasks with no interdependency run concurrently\n- **Queued** — tasks assigned to queue groups (one consumer per group)\n- **Retried** — failed tasks re-attempted with backoff\n\n---\n\n## 2. Execution Primitives\n\n### 2.1 Parallel Execution\n\n**Mechanism**: NATS broadcast fan-out.\n\n**Usage**: When a plan contains independent tasks (no `DependsOn`).\n\n**Flow**:\n```\nPlanner creates plan with tasks T1, T2 (parallel)\n    │\n    ▼\nExecutor publishes T1 → ethan.capability.docker.build\nExecutor publishes T2 → ethan.capability.docker.publish\n    │\n    ▼\nBoth modules receive and execute concurrently\n    │\n    ▼\nExecutor collects all results via subscription callbacks\n    │\n    ▼\nExecutor aggregates → plan.done (when all tasks complete or fail)\n```\n\n**Implementation (Go goroutines)**:\n```go\nfunc (e *Executor) ExecuteParallel(tasks []Task) []TaskResult {\n    var wg sync.WaitGroup\n    results := make([]TaskResult, len(tasks))\n\n    for i, task := range tasks {\n        wg.Add(1)\n        go func(idx int, t Task) {\n            defer wg.Done()\n            results[idx] = e.runTask(t)\n        }(i, task)\n    }\n    wg.Wait()\n    return results\n}\n```\n\n### 2.2 Queued Events\n\n**Mechanism**: NATS queue groups (load-balanced consumers).\n\n**Usage**: Task assignment to module instances (one instance handles each task).\n\n**Configuration**: All modules subscribed to `ethan.executor.task.assigned` with queue group `module-<capability>`.\n\n**Properties**:\n- Exactly one consumer per message (within queue group)\n- Automatic load balancing across instance\n- If instance crashes, message is re-delivered to another instance\n\n**Example**:\n```\nNATS subject: ethan.executor.task.assigned\nQueue group:  module-docker-build\n\nModule A (subscribed) → receives message, starts task\nModule B (subscribed) → idle (next message)\n\nIf Module A crashes → NATS redelivers to Module B\n```\n\n### 2.3 Cancellation\n\n**Mechanism**: `task.cancel` event with correlation matching.\n\n**Cancellation sources**:\n- User request (interface sends cancel)\n- Timeout (executor detects deadline exceeded)\n- Dependency failure (upstream task failed)\n\n**Flow**:\n```\n1. Executor receives cancellation request\n2. Executor publishes ethan.executor.task.cancelled\n3. Module receives cancel event, stops processing\n4. Module publishes ethan.executor.task.completed with status \"cancelled\"\n5. Executor marks plan as cancelled\n```\n\n**Implementation**:\n```go\ntype CancellationToken struct {\n    mu         sync.Mutex\n    cancelled  bool\n    onCancel   []func()\n}\n\nfunc (c *CancellationToken) Cancel() {\n    c.mu.Lock()\n    defer c.mu.Unlock()\n    c.cancelled = true\n    for _, f := range c.onCancel {\n        f()\n    }\n}\n\nfunc (e *Executor) ExecuteCancellable(task Task, ctx CancellationToken) TaskResult {\n    select {\n    case result := <-e.runTaskAsync(task):\n        return result\n    case <-ctx.Done():\n        return TaskResult{TaskID: task.ID, Status: \"cancelled\"}\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### 2.4 Retry Mechanism\n\n**Mechanism**: Exponential backoff with configurable max retries.\n\n**Retry policy** (configured per task type):\n```json\n{\n  \"retry_policy\": {\n    \"max_retries\": 3,\n    \"initial_delay_ms\": 1000,\n    \"backoff_factor\": 2.0,\n    \"max_delay_ms\": 30000\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**Flow**:\n```\nTask fails (status=error)\n    │\n    ▼\nCheck retries < max_retries?\n    │\n    ├─ YES:\n    │     ▼\n    │   Wait = initial_delay * (backoff_factor ^ attempt)\n    │   Wait = min(Wait, max_delay)\n    │   Sleep(Wait)\n    │   Publish ethan.executor.task.retrying\n    │   Re-publish task\n    │\n    └─ NO:\n          ▼\n        Mark task as permanently failed\n        Publish ethan.executor.task.failed\n```\n\n**Implementation**:\n```go\nfunc (e *Executor) runTaskWithRetry(task Task) TaskResult {\n    attempt := 0\n    for {\n        result := e.runTask(task)\n        if result.Status != \"error\" || attempt >= task.MaxRetries {\n            return result\n        }\n        attempt++\n        delay := time.Duration(float64(time.Second) * math.Pow(2, float64(attempt))) // 1s, 2s, 4s\n        if delay > 30*time.Second {\n            delay = 30 * time.Second\n        }\n        e.bus.Publish(SubjectExecutorTaskRetrying, mustMarshal(TaskResult{\n            TaskID:   task.ID,\n            Status:   \"retrying\",\n            Duration: delay,\n        }))\n        time.Sleep(delay)\n    }\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. Execution Pipeline\n\n```\nRequest received\n    │\n    ▼\nPlanner decomposes into ExecutionPlan\n    │\n    ▼\nExecutor receives plan\n    │\n    ├─► Partition tasks by dependency\n    │      │\n    │      ├─ Level 0: tasks with no dependencies (parallel batch)\n    │      ├─ Level 1: tasks depending on Level 0\n    │      └─ Level N: tasks depending on Level N-1\n    │\n    ├─► For each level:\n    │      │\n    │      ├─► Execute tasks in parallel (goroutines)\n    │      │      │\n    │      │      ├─► Publish task.assigned → queue group\n    │      │      ├─► Wait for completion with timeout\n    │      │      ├─► Retry on failure (up to max_retries)\n    │      │      └─► Collect results\n    │      │\n    │      └─► If any task fails → cancel remaining tasks in level\n    │\n    └─► Aggregate all results → plan.done\n```\n\n---\n\n## 4. Event Subjects\n\n### 4.1 Task Events\n\n| Subject | Payload | When |\n|---------|---------|------|\n| `ethan.executor.task.assigned` | `{task_id, capability, params, retry_count}` | Task dispatched to module |\n| `ethan.executor.task.running` | `{task_id}` | Module acknowledges start |\n| `ethan.executor.task.completed` | `{task_id, result, duration_ms}` | Module returns success |\n| `ethan.executor.task.failed` | `{task_id, error, attempt}` | Max retries exceeded |\n| `ethan.executor.task.timeout` | `{task_id, timeout_ms}` | Deadline exceeded |\n| `ethan.executor.task.retrying` | `{task_id, delay_ms}` | Retry attempt scheduled |\n| `ethan.executor.task.cancelled` | `{task_id, reason}` | Task cancelled |\n| `ethan.executor.plan.done` | `{plan_id, results[], total_duration}` | All tasks complete |\n\n### 4.2 Queue Group Configuration\n\n| Subject | Queue Group | Purpose |\n|---------|------------|---------|\n| `ethan.executor.task.assigned.docker.build` | `module-docker-build` | Load balance Docker build tasks |\n| `ethan.executor.task.assigned.docker.publish` | `module-docker-publish` | Load balance Docker publish tasks |\n| `ethan.executor.task.assigned.memory.store` | `module-memory` | Load balance memory stores |\n| `ethan.executor.task.assigned.*` | `module-<capability>` | Dynamic per capability |\n\n---\n\n## 5. Timeouts\n\nEach task has two timeout levels:\n\n| Level | Duration | Action |\n|-------|----------|--------|\n| **Soft** | `task.timeout` (configurable, default 30s) | Log warning, continue waiting |\n| **Hard** | `task.timeout * 1.5` | Emit `task.timeout`, cancel task |\n\n**Hard timeout flow**:\n```\n1. Executor starts timer when task.assigned is published\n2. If hard timeout expires → publish executor.task.timeout\n3. Executor marks task as failed (status: timeout)\n4. If module later completes → result is discarded\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. Task Dependency Resolution\n\nThe executor uses topological sort to determine task execution order.\n\n**Algorithm**:\n```go\nfunc resolveDependencies(tasks []Task) [][]Task {\n    // 1. Build in-degree map, adjacency list\n    indegree := make(map[string]int)\n    next := make(map[string][]string)\n    taskMap := make(map[string]Task)\n\n    for _, t := range tasks {\n        taskMap[t.ID] = t\n        if _, ok := indegree[t.ID]; !ok {\n            indegree[t.ID] = 0\n        }\n        for _, dep := range t.DependsOn {\n            next[dep] = append(next[dep], t.ID)\n            indegree[t.ID]++\n        }\n    }\n\n    // 2. Topological sort into levels\n    var levels [][]Task\n    queue := []string{}\n    for id, deg := range indegree {\n        if deg == 0 {\n            queue = append(queue, id)\n        }\n    }\n\n    for len(queue) > 0 {\n        level := []Task{}\n        var nextQueue []string\n        for _, id := range queue {\n            level = append(level, taskMap[id])\n            for _, nid := range next[id] {\n                indegree[nid]--\n                if indegree[nid] == 0 {\n                    nextQueue = append(nextQueue, nid)\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        levels = append(levels, level)\n        queue = nextQueue\n    }\n\n    return levels\n}\n```\n\n**Example**:\n```\nTasks: [A, B, C, D]\nDependencies: C → A, D → B, D → C\n\nLevel 0: [A, B]       (parallel)\nLevel 1: [C]          (depends on A)\nLevel 2: [D]          (depends on B, C)\n```\n\n---\n\n## 7. Cancellation Propagation\n\nWhen a task is cancelled, all downstream tasks are also cancelled.\n\n**Flow**:\n```\nTask A fails → Executor emits task.cancelled for A\n    │\n    ▼\nExecutor checks: which tasks depend on A?\n    │\n    ▼\nTasks B, C (depends on A) → cancelled (not assigned)\n    │\n    ▼\nTasks D, E (depends on B) → cancelled (never started)\n    │\n    ▼\nPlan result: partially failed\n```\n\n---\n\n## 8. Retry Configuration\n\nPer-capability retry defaults (overridable by task params):\n\n```json\n{\n  \"docker.build\": {\n    \"max_retries\": 2,\n    \"initial_delay_ms\": 2000,\n    \"backoff_factor\": 2.0,\n    \"max_delay_ms\": 30000\n  },\n  \"web.fetch\": {\n    \"max_retries\": 3,\n    \"initial_delay_ms\": 1000,\n    \"backoff_factor\": 1.5,\n    \"max_delay_ms\": 15000\n  },\n  \"memory.store\": {\n    \"max_retries\": 1,\n    \"initial_delay_ms\": 500,\n    \"backoff_factor\": 1.0,\n    \"max_delay_ms\": 5000\n  }\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 9. Concurrency Model Summary\n\n| Feature | Mechanism | Scope |\n|---------|-----------|-------|\n| Parallel tasks | Go goroutines + `sync.WaitGroup` | Per-plan (Level 0 tasks execute together) |\n| Queue groups | NATS queue groups | Load balance across module instances |\n| Cancellation | `context.Context` + cancel events | Per-task, propagates to dependents |\n| Retry | Exponential backoff loop | Per-task, configurable per capability |\n| Timeouts | `time.After` + cancel | Per-task, hard timeout = soft * 1.5 |\n| Ordering | Topological sort | Per-plan task DAG |","operationIsLocatedInWorkspace":true,"startLineNumbers":[]}

; attempt++ {\n\t\tresult := e.runTask(task)\n\t\tif result.Status != \"error\" || attempt >= policy.MaxRetries {\n\t\t\treturn result\n\t\t}\n\t\tdelay := policy.WaitDuration(attempt)\n\t\tretryEv := types.NewEvent(\"executor.task.retrying\", \"executor\", map[string]any{\n\t\t\t\"task_id\":  task.ID,\n\t\t\t\"attempt\":  attempt + 1,\n\t\t\t\"delay_ms\": delay.Milliseconds(),\n\t\t}, nil)\n\t\tdata, _ := json.Marshal(retryEv)\n\t\tbus.Publish(\"ethan.executor.task.retrying\", data)\n\t\ttime.Sleep(delay)\n\t}\n}\n\n// ExecuteParallel runs tasks concurrently using goroutines.\nfunc (e *Executor) ExecuteParallel(tasks []planner.Task) []TaskResult {\n\tresults := make([]TaskResult, len(tasks))\n\tdone := make(chan struct{}, len(tasks))\n\n\tfor i, task := range tasks {\n\t\tgo func(idx int, t planner.Task) {\n\t\t\tresults[idx] = e.RunTaskWithRetry(t, e.bus)\n\t\t\tdone <- struct{}{}\n\t\t}(i, task)\n\t}\n\n\tfor range tasks {\n\t\t<-done\n\t}\n\treturn results\n}","operationIsLocatedInWorkspace":true,"startLineNumbers":[]}

Every character must feel intentional. No clutter. No noise. Premium developer tool.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Color System\n\n### 1.1 Palette (16 ANSI, terminal-safe)\n\n```\nETHAN Blue      \\033[38;5;39m  │ Primary accent, brand identity\nETHAN Cyan      \\033[38;5;44m  │ Information, data, neutral context\nETHAN Green     \\033[38;5;42m  │ Success, confirmation, ready state\nETHAN Yellow    \\033[38;5;220m │ Warnings, attention required\nETHAN Red       \\033[38;5;196m │ Errors, failures, critical\nETHAN Purple    \\033[38;5;135m │ Thinking, reasoning, meta\nETHAN Dim       \\033[38;5;245m │ Secondary text, metadata, timestamps\nETHAN White     \\033[38;5;255m │ Primary text\nETHAN Bold      \\033[1m        │ Only for emphasis, never for decoration\nETHAN Reset     \\033[0m        │ Back to terminal default\n```\n\n### 1.2 Usage Rules\n\n| Element | Color | Why |\n|---------|-------|-----|\n| Brand prefix `◆` | Blue | Primary identity marker |\n| Prompts `>` | Blue | Active input state |\n| Status indicators | Green / Yellow / Red | At-a-glance system state |\n| Thinking indicator | Purple | Active cognitive processing |\n| Timestamps | Dim | Present but not distracting |\n| Errors | Red + Bold | Cannot be missed |\n| Success confirmations | Green on new line | Positive reinforcement |\n| User input | White | Neutral, readable |\n| System output | Cyan | Differentiated from user text |\n| File paths | Cyan + Dim | Technical but secondary |\n\n### 1.3 What NOT to do\n\n- No blinking text\n- No background colors (terminal compatibility)\n- No more than 2 colors per line\n- No color gradients or 24-bit (fails on basic terminals)\n\n---\n\n## 2. Typography & Spacing\n\n### 2.1 Prompt Line\n\n```\n◆  ethan  ◇  working  ▸\n```\n\n**Anatomy**:\n```\n◆           — brand marker (blue)\nethan       — system name (bold white)\n◇           — separator (dim)\nworking     — state badge (cyan)\n▸           — input cursor (blue)\n```\n\n**State badges**:\n| State | Badge | Color |\n|-------|-------|-------|\n| Ready | `idle` | Green |\n| Processing | `working` | Cyan |\n| Error | `error` | Red |\n| Thinking | `thinking` | Purple |\n| Autonomous | `auto` | Cyan |\n\n### 2.2 Output Blocks\n\n```\n◆  Result                     <- header (blue), blank line before\n✓ Deployed 3 services         <- content (white)\n  → api-gateway               <- sub-item (cyan, indent 2 spaces)\n  → user-service\n  → notification\n  ⏱ 2.3s                      <- metadata (dim), new line\n\n◆  Error                      <- error header (red)\n✗ Connection refused           <- error message (red)\n  → host: localhost:4222       <- context (dim)\n  → try: ethan daemon start    <- suggestion (cyan)\n```\n\n### 2.3 Spacing Rules\n\n- 1 blank line before every `◆` section\n- 0 blank lines between bullet items\n- 1 blank line after sections (except last)\n- 2-space indent for sub-items\n- 4-space indent for code/data blocks\n\n### 2.4 Line Width\n\n- Max 120 characters (hard wrap at word boundary)\n- Break long lines with `↳  ` (3-space continuation indent)\n\n```\n◆  Long output that exceeds the maximum line width and needs to\n↳  be wrapped with continuation indent for readability\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. Prompt Modes\n\n### 3.1 Single Command Mode\n\n```\n◆  ethan  ◇  idle  ▸ build docker\n```\n\n### 3.2 Interactive Chat Mode\n\n```\n◆  ethan  ◇  chat  ▸\n```\n\nRaw input line. No prefix per message. History accessible with ↑↓.\n\n### 3.3 Streaming Mode (thinking)\n\n```\n◆  ethan  ◇  thinking  ▸\n\n  ■  Querying capability registry...\n  ■  Found docker.build (v1.0.0)\n  ■  Deploying service...\n  ✓  Complete (3.2s)\n```\n\nSpinner animation on `■` (rotates through `◐◓◑◒` during work).\n\n---\n\n## 4. Output Formatting Rules\n\n### 4.1 Status Messages\n\n```\n✓  OK                        # success (green)\n✗  FAILED                    # error (red)\n⚠  WARNING                   # warning (yellow)\nℹ  INFO                      # info (cyan)\n○  OFFLINE                   # offline state (dim)\n●  ONLINE                    # online state (green)\n◆  SECTION                   # section header (blue)\n→  ITEM                      # list item (cyan)\n↳  CONTINUATION              # line wrap (dim + indent)\n```\n\n### 4.2 Timing & Metadata\n\nAlways on the last line of a section, in dim. Format: `⏱ <duration><unit>` or `@ <timestamp>`.\n\n```\n◆  Result\n✓ System online\n  → 3 modules active\n  ⏱ 1.2s\n```\n\n### 4.3 Structured Data\n\n```json\n{\n  \"key\": \"value\"\n}\n```\n\n- Preceded by `◆  Data` header\n- Syntax-highlighted with minimal color (keys cyan, values white, strings dim)\n- Max 20 lines, truncate with `… (+N more)`\n\n### 4.4 Errors\n\n```\n◆  Error\n✗ <error title>              <- bold red\n  → <context>                 <- dim\n  → <suggestion>              <- cyan\n```\n\nAlways include a suggestion line when possible. Never show raw stack traces.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Progress Indicators\n\n### 5.1 Spinner\n\n```\n  ◐  Loading...\n  ◓\n  ◑\n  ◒\n```\n\nCharacters: `◐◓◑◒` — rotates clockwise. Placed at column 0, 2-space indent.\n\n### 5.2 Progress Bar\n\nOnly for operations with known total (installing, downloading):\n\n```\n  [████████░░░░]  67%  (3/5 plugins installed)\n```\n\n- 8 block characters wide\n- Filled: `█` (dark), Empty: `░` (dim)\n- Percentage on the right\n- Description in dim\n\n### 5.3 Stepped Progress\n\nFor multi-step operations:\n\n```\n◆  Installing plugin\n  ✓  Copied files            (0.3s)\n  ✓  Installed dependencies   (2.1s)\n  ✓  Validated capabilities   (0.1s)\n  ✓  Registered commands      (0.0s)\n  ✓  Complete                 (2.5s)\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. Special Modes\n\n### 6.1 Thinking Mode\n\nWhen ETHAN is processing (LLM call, planning), show a purple thinking section:\n\n```\n◆  ethan  ◇  thinking  ▸ deploy\n\n  ■  Analyzing intent...\n  ■  Decomposing goal into tasks\n  ■  Querying docker.build capability\n  ✓  Complete\n```\n\nThe `■` character animates as a spinner during active processing. Results appear in real time.\n\n### 6.2 Confirmation Mode\n\nFor destructive operations:\n\n```\n◆  Confirm\n  Destroy production database? [y/N] ▸\n```\n\n- `y` = green confirmation message\n- Anything else = red \"Cancelled\"\n- Timeout after 30s = `⚠  Timeout, assuming no`\n\n### 6.3 Suggest Mode (autocomplete)\n\n```\n◆  ethan  ◇  idle  ▸ status\n\n  Did you mean?\n  → ethan status\n  → ethan daemon status\n  → ethan service status\n```\n\n---\n\n## 7. Theme Implementation\n\n### 7.1 Color Constants\n\nFile: `cli/core/colors.py`\n\n```python\nclass C:\n    RESET   = \"\\033[0m\"\n    BOLD    = \"\\033[1m\"\n    DIM     = \"\\033[2m\"\n    BLUE    = \"\\033[38;5;39m\"\n    CYAN    = \"\\033[38;5;44m\"\n    GREEN   = \"\\033[38;5;42m\"\n    YELLOW  = \"\\033[38;5;220m\"\n    RED     = \"\\033[38;5;196m\"\n    PURPLE  = \"\\033[38;5;135m\"\n    WHITE   = \"\\033[38;5;255m\"\n```\n\n### 7.2 Icon Constants\n\n```python\nclass I:\n    CHECK   = \"✓\"\n    CROSS   = \"✗\"\n    WARN    = \"⚠\"\n    INFO    = \"ℹ\"\n    ARROW   = \"→\"\n    WRAP    = \"↳\"\n    SECTION = \"◆\"\n    SPINNER = [\"◐\", \"◓\", \"◑\", \"◒\"]\n    TIMER   = \"⏱\"\n    DOT     = \"●\"\n    CIRCL   = \"○\"\n    INPUT   = \"▸\"\n```\n\n### 7.3 Formatter Functions\n\n```python\ndef section(title):\n    return f\"{C.BLUE}{I.SECTION} {title}{C.RESET}\"\n\ndef success(msg):\n    return f\"  {C.GREEN}{I.CHECK} {msg}{C.RESET}\"\n\ndef error(title, context=None, suggestion=None):\n    lines = [f\"{C.RED}{I.CROSS} {title}{C.RESET}\"]\n    if context:\n        lines.append(f\"  {C.DIM}{I.ARROW} {context}{C.RESET}\")\n    if suggestion:\n        lines.append(f\"  {C.CYAN}{I.ARROW} {suggestion}{C.RESET}\")\n    return \"\\n\".join(lines)\n\ndef metadata(text):\n    return f\"  {C.DIM}{I.TIMER} {text}{C.RESET}\"\n\ndef prompt(state=\"idle\"):\n    color = {\"idle\": C.GREEN, \"working\": C.CYAN, \"error\": C.RED, \"thinking\": C.PURPLE}\n    badge = color.get(state, C.CYAN)\n    return f\"{C.BLUE}{I.SECTION}{C.RESET}  {C.BOLD}ethan{C.RESET}  {badge}{state}{C.RESET}  {C.BLUE}{I.INPUT}{C.RESET} \"\n```\n\n---\n\n## 8. Anti-Patterns (forbidden)\n\n| Pattern | Why |\n|---------|-----|\n| `>>>` prompts | Python REPL, not cognitive runtime |\n| `$` prompts | Shell, not ETHAN |\n| Bold everywhere | Only for emphasis, never decoration |\n| Rainbow colors | Unprofessional, terminal-incompatible |\n| Progress bars for unknown durations | Misleading |\n| Stack traces shown raw | Use structured error blocks |\n| Inconsistent icon spacing | 2-space indent always |","operationIsLocatedInWorkspace":true,"startLineNumbers":[]}

The terminal should feel alive.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Rendering Model\n\n### 1.1 In-place line update\n\n```\nBefore: ⠋ ethan  Processing...\nAfter:  ⠋ ethan  Querying registry...\n```\n\nSame line, same indentation, same color. Only text changes.\n\n**Rules**:\n- Same cursor position (no line breaks unless the model emits `\\n`)\n- ANSI escape sequence: `\\033[<n>G` (move cursor to column n) or `\\r` (carriage return)\n- After finishing, print `\\n` once\n\n### 1.2 Mode 1: Streaming (preferred)\n\n```python\nstreamer = Streamer()\nstreamer.start(\"Thinking...\")\n\nfor chunk in response_stream:\n    streamer.write(chunk)\n\nstreamer.done()\n```\n\nOutput (`\\r` returns cursor to line start):\n```\n⠋ ethan  Thinking...                         ← initial\n⠋ ethan  Querying registry...               ← update\n⠋ ethan  Building task plan...              ← update\n⠋ ethan  Done                               ← update\n                                              ← final \\n after done()\n```\n\n### 1.3 Mode 2: Buffered (fallback)\n\nIf streaming fails (API doesn't support `text/event-stream`):\n```python\nstreamer = Streamer()\nstreamer.start(\"Thinking...\")\n\n# Blocker: API blocks, no chunks\nresponse_text = send_sync(msg)\nstreamer.write(response_text)  # single write, looks smooth\nstreamer.done()\n```\n\n### 1.4 Mode 3: Offline (last resort)\n\nNetwork error:\n```\n⠋ ethan  Connection lost\n✗ Streaming interrupted — falling back to batch result\n```\n\n---\n\n## 2. Cancellation (CTRL+C)\n\n```\n1. User presses CTRL+C\n2. Streamer raises KeyboardInterrupt-safe signal\n3. Current line is cleared\n4. Partial output is preserved (not rolled back)\n5. Streamer enters cancelled state\n6. Caller handles cancellation gracefully\n```\n\n```\n⠋ ethan  Processing...  [CTRL+C]\n⠋ ethan  Cancelled\n```\n(streamer keeps partial text for context; caller decides to retry, ignore, or abort)\n\n---\n\n## 3. Smoothness Guarantees\n\n| Property | Mechanism |\n|----------|-----------|\n| **No flicker** | Write to same line, same escape sequence, no cursor jump |\n| **No tearing** | Flush after every chunk (`sys.stdout.flush()`) |\n| **No double-write** | Track `last_len`, clear only extra characters |\n| **Stable cursor** | Keep cursor at end of text after every update |\n\n### 3.1 Double-write prevention\n\n```python\nclass Streamer:\n    def write(self, chunk):\n        new_text = self.current + chunk\n        # Erase only what we previously wrote\n        sys.stdout.write(\"\\r\" + \" \" * self._last_len + \"\\r\")\n        # Write new text\n        sys.stdout.write(new_text)\n        self._last_len = len(new_text)\n        sys.stdout.flush()\n```\n\n### 3.2 Spinner integration\n\n```\n  ◐ Thinking...  (animated spinner, rotates every 200ms)\n```\n\nSpinner runs in a background thread (or async task). Text is drawn at fixed column after spinner.\n\n---\n\n## 4. State Machine\n\n```\nIDLE → STREAMING → DONE\n         │         │\n         │         └──► ERROR (fallback)\n         │\n         └──► CANCELLED (CTRL+C)\n```\n\n| State | Display | Action |\n|-------|---------|--------|\n| IDLE | (none) | Ready to stream |\n| STREAMING | `⠋ ethan  <accumulated_text>` | Receiving chunks |\n| DONE | `⠋ ethan  <full_text>` then newline | Completed |\n| CANCELLED | `⠋ ethan  Cancelled` | Interrupted by user |\n| FALLBACK | Static prompt → batch text | If stream fails |\n\n---\n\n## 5. Public API\n\n```python\nclass Streamer:\n    def start(self, hint: str = \"Thinking...\") -> None:\n        \"\"\"Begin stream. Prints initial line with spinner.\"\"\"\n        ...\n\n    def write(self, chunk: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Append chunk and re-render smoothly.\"\"\"\n        ...\n\n    def done(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Finalize stream. Print final \\n.\"\"\"\n        ...\n\n    def cancel(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Cancel stream. Print 'Cancelled', preserve context.\"\"\"\n        ...\n\n    def fallback(self, text: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"If streaming fails, replace with static text.\"\"\"\n        ...\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. Integration Points\n\n| Component | Uses |\n|-----------|------|\n| `chat.py` | Streamer for assistant responses |\n| `cli/commands/run.py` | Streamer for long-running task */\n| `cli/commands/exec.py` | Streamer for command output |\n\n---\n\n## 7. Error Recovery\n\n```\nStreaming error (network, timeout, protocol)\n    │\n    ▼\nStreamer.fallback(error_message)\n    │\n    ▼\nShow compact error + retry choice\n```\n\n```\n⠋ ethan  Stream interrupted\n✗ Connection lost — retrying in 2s...               [fallback]\n\n✓ Reconnected — resuming stream                      [recovered]\n⠋ ethan  Resume querying...\n```\n\n---\n\n## 8. Token vs Chunk\n\n**Token-by-token**:\n- `for token in llm.stream(...): streamer.write(token)`\n- Smoothest, most responsive\n- Requires SSE / WebSocket from API\n\n**Chunk**:\n- `for chunk in response.iter_content(1024): streamer.write(chunk)`\n- Good enough for most cases\n- Works with plain HTTP streaming\n\n**Batch**:\n- `streamer.write(response_text)`\n- Fallback only\n\n---\n\n## 9. Example in chat.py\n\n```python\ndef send_with_stream(msg, session_id):\n    streamer = Streamer()\n    streamer.start()\n\n    try:\n        for chunk in client.stream(msg, session_id):\n            streamer.write(chunk)\n        streamer.done()\n    except KeyboardInterrupt:\n        streamer.cancel()\n        return None, \"cancelled\"\n    except Exception as e:\n        streamer.fallback(str(e))\n        raise\n\n    mem.record(session_id, \"assistant\", streamer.text)\n    return streamer.text, streamer.latency\n\n```\n\n---\n\n## 10. Future: Markdown/Code awareness\n\n```\n⠋ ethan  Sure. Shows initial line.\"\"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            self._start_time = time.time()\n            self._cancelled = False\n            self._phase = 0\n            self.text = \"\"\n            self._last_len = 0\n        self._start_spinner()\n        self.write(hint)\n\n    def write(self, chunk: str):\n        \"\"\"Append chunk and re-render.\"\"\"\n        if self._cancelled:\n            return\n        with self._lock:\n            self.text += chunk\n            display = self.text\n        # Clear previous line\n        sys.stdout.write(\"\\r\" + \" \" * self._last_len + \"\\r\")\n        # Write new text\n        sys.stdout.write(display)\n        self._last_len = len(display)\n        sys.stdout.flush()\n\n    def done(self):\n        \"\"\"Finalize stream.\"\"\"\n        self._stop_spinner()\n        sys.stdout.write(\"\\n\")\n        sys.stdout.flush()\n\n    def cancel(self):\n        \"\"\"Cancel stream on user interrupt.\"\"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            self._cancelled = True\n        self._stop_spinner()\n        # Clear and show cancelled state\n        sys.stdout.write(\"\\r\" + \" \" * self._last_len + \"\\r\")\n        sys.stdout.flush()\n        sys.stdout.write(f\"{clr.PURPLE}{clr.I.DOT} ethan{C.RESET}  {clr.YELLOW}Cancelled{C.RESET}\\n\")\n        sys.stdout.flush()\n        self.text += \" [cancelled]\"\n\n    def fallback(self, text: str):\n        \"\"\"If streaming fails, replace with static error.\"\"\"\n        self._stop_spinner()\n        sys.stdout.write(\"\\r\" + \" \" * self._last_len + \"\\r\")\n        sys.stdout.flush()\n        sys.stdout.write(f\"{clr.RED}{clr.I.CROSS} Streaming failed{C.RESET}\\n\")\n        sys.stdout.write(f\"  {clr.DIM}{text}{C.RESET}\\n\")\n        sys.stdout.flush()\n        sys.stdout.write(f\"  {clr.CYAN}{clr.I.ARROW} Falling back to batch result{C.RESET}\\n\")\n        sys.stdout.flush()\n\n    def _start_spinner(self):\n        if self._spin_thread is not None:\n            return\n        self._spinning = True\n        self._spin_thread = threading.Thread(target=self._spin_loop, daemon=True)\n        self._spin_thread.start()\n\n    def _stop_spinner(self):\n        self._spinning = False\n        self._spin_thread = None\n\n    def _spin_loop(self):\n        chars = clr.I.SPINNER\n        while self._spinning:\n            with self._lock:\n                if self._cancelled:\n                    break\n                current = self.text\n                last_len = self._last_len\n            # Every error teaches. Every hint guides.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Command Grammar\n\n### 1.1 Structure\n\n```\nethan <command> [args...] [flags...]\n```\n\nMinimal verbs, maximum clarity.\n\n### 1.2 Core Commands\n\n| Command | Purpose | Examples |\n|---------|---------|---------|\n| `ethan chat` | Interactive AI chat | `ethan chat`, `ethan chat --resume` |\n| `ethan run <cmd>` | Execute a command in a capability | `ethan run docker build`, `ethan run pytest` |\n| `ethan status` | Show kernel/system state | `ethan status`, `ethan status --verbose` |\n| `ethan logs` | Tail system logs | `ethan logs --follow`, `ethan logs --lines 50` |\n| `ethan plugin <sub>` | Manage plugins | `ethan plugin list`, `ethan plugin install <path>` |\n| `ethan shell` | Drop into ethan-shell | `ethan shell` |\n| `ethan help` | Show help | `ethan help`, `ethan help chat` |\n\n---\n\n## 2. Autocomplete Hints\n\n### 2.1 Inline Suggestions (TAB)\n\n```\n◆  ethan  ◇  idle  ▸ ru<TAB>\n                                └─► autocomplete to \"run\"\n```\n\n**Behavior**:\n- Single TAB: complete to longest common prefix\n- Double TAB: show all matches\n- No match: bell (BEL char `\\a`)\n\n### 2.2 Context Suggestions\n\n```\n◆  ethan  ◇  idle  ▸ run\n   Did you mean?               ← shown when no exact match\n   → ethan run\n   → ethan shell\n   → ethan status\n```\n\nTriggered when:\n- Command not found\n- User pauses (200ms silence after typing)\n\n### 2.3 Argument Suggestions\n\n```\n◆  ethan  ◇  idle  ▸ plugin <TAB>\n   Commands: install  list  remove  info\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. Inline Help (--help)\n\n### 3.1 Minimal Help (default)\n\n```\n◆  ethan  ◇  idle  ▸ chat --help\n\n  ethan chat — interactive AI chat\n\n  Usage:\n    ethan chat              Start new session\n    ethan chat --resume     Resume last session\n\n  Flags:\n    -r, --resume            Resume previous session\n    -h, --help              Show this help\n```\n\n### 3.2 Top-level Help\n\n```\n◆  ethan  ◇  idle  ▸ --help\n\n  ETHAN — Cognitive Runtime CLI\n\n  Commands:\n    chat       Interactive AI chat\n    run        Execute a command via capabilities\n    status     Show system state\n    logs       Tail system logs\n    plugin     Manage plugins\n    shell      Open ethan-shell\n    help        Show help\n\n  Flags:\n    -v, --version    Show version\n    -h, --help       Show this help\n```\n\n### 3.3 Rules\n\n- Max 4 lines per command description\n-Flags indented under \"Flags:\"\n- Examples shown only for complex commands\n- Never show full man page by default\n\n---\n\n## 4. Load all command names into a list\n2. Calculate Levenshtein distance between input and each command\n3. If distance <= 2 (for short) or <= 3 (for long), suggest it\n4. Show best match first\n\n### 4.2 Substring Match\n\n```\nInput:  ethan pla\nSuggestion: Did you mean?\n  → ethan plugin list\n  → ethan plugin install\n```\n\nIf input is a prefix of multiple commands, show all matches.\n\n### 4.3 Phonetic Match (Soundex)\n\nFuture: handle phonetic typos (`ethan shel` → `ethan shell`).\n\n---\n\n## 5. Smart Error Messages\n\n### 5.1 Unknown Command\n\n```\n◆  ethan  ◇  idle  ▸ strat\n\n✗ Unknown command: 'strat'\n  → Did you mean? ethan status\n  → Try: ethan --help\n```\n\n### 5.2 Missing Argument\n\n```\n◆  ethan  ◇  idle  ▸ run\n\n✗ Missing argument: <command>\n  → Usage: ethan run <cmd>\n  → Example: ethan run docker build\n```\n\n### 5.3 Failed Command\n\n```\n◆  ethan  ◇  idle  ▸ run docker build\n\n✗ Command failed: docker build\n  → Exit code 1\n  → Context: /app\n  → Try: ethan logs --follow\n```\n\n### 5.4 API Unreachable\n\n```\n◆  ethan  ◇  error  ▸ status\n\n✗ API unreachable\n  → ethan daemon may be stopped\n  → try: ethan daemon start\n```\n\n### 5.5 Permission Denied\n\n```\n✗ Permission denied\n  → plugin \"danger\" requires admin level\n  → Run as: sudo ethan plugin install danger\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. Implementation\n\n### 6.1 UX Module\n\nFile: `cli/core/ux.py`\n\n```python\nclass UX:\n    @staticmethod\n    def suggest_command(input_str: str, commands: list[str]) -> str | None:\n        \"\"\"Return best matching command or None.\"\"\"\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def levenshtein(a: str, b: str) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Calculate edit distance.\"\"\"\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def show_help(topic: str | None = None) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Display minimal help.\"\"\"\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def smart_error(kind: str, **context) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Generate actionable error block.\"\"\"\n```\n\n### 6.2 Integration\n\nEvery command handler should:\n1. Validate args\n2. On failure: call `UX.smart_error()`\n3. On unknown command: call `UX.suggest_command()`\n\n---\n\n## 7. UX Patterns Reference\n\n| Situation | Response |\n|-----------|----------|\n| Unknown command | Suggest closest match + `--help` |\n| Missing required arg | Show usage + example |\n| Flag not recognized | Show valid flags |\n| Command not available | Show install command (for plugins) |\n| API error | Show actionable recovery message |\n| KeyboardInterrupt | Graceful exit with \"Cancelled\" |\n| Empty input | No feedback (silent) |\n| Long output | Paginate or offer `--less` flag |\n\n---\n\n## 8. Anti-Patterns\n\n| Pattern | Why |\n|---------|-----|\n| \"Error: invalid input\" | Not actionable — tell user what's valid |\n| Stack traces by default | Use structured errors; show trace with `--debug` |\n| \"Usage: ethan <cmd> [args]\" | Too vague — show specific command usage |\n| Multiple errors at once | User can't parse; show first error, stop |\n| CAPS LOCK emphasis | Only bold + color; never SHOUT |\n| Silent failures | Always print something (error or hint) |\n\n---\n\n## Appendix A: UX Copy Guidelines\n\n- **Tone**: helpful colleague, not robot\n- **Length**: 1-2 lines max for errors\n- **Action**: every error ends with a suggestion or next step\n- **Humor**: minimal, never at user's frustration\n- **Consistency**: same wording for same concepts (`try:`, `Usage:`, `Example:`)\n\n---\n\n## Appendix B: Minimal Help Format\n\n```\n<verb> — <one-line description>\n\nUsage:\n  ethan <verb> <required> [optional]\n\nFlags:\n  -x, --flag    Description\n  -h, --help    Show help\n```","operationIsLocatedInWorkspace":true,"startLineNumbers":[]}

Context-aware. Proactive.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Intent Detection\n\n### 1.1 Input Classification\n\n```\nUser input\n    │\n    ▼\nClassify into one of:\n  [COMMAND]        — exact match to known command (run, status, logs, etc.)\n  [INTENT]         — action-oriented phrase (fix docker, deploy app)\n  [CHAT]           — conversational (hello, explain X)\n  [SMART_CMD]      — short command shorthand (logs → ethan logs)\n```\n\n### 1.2 SHOT Parameter Detection\n\nExtract key-value parameters from natural language:\n\n| Input | Detected |\n|-------|----------|\n| `fix docker` | intent=fix, target=docker |\n| `check api health` | intent=check, target=api, aspect=health |\n| `deploy to staging` | intent=deploy, env=staging |\n| `run pytest in /app` | intent=run, cmd=pytest, cwd=/app |\n\nPattern matching:\n- `run <cmd>` → execute command\n- `fix <target>` → diagnostic + repair\n- `check <target>` → health check\n- `deploy <target> to <env>` → deploy\n- `logs [for <service>]` → tail logs\n\n---\n\n## 2. Smart Command Execution\n\n### 2.1 Auto-Execution\n\nWhen an intent maps 1:1 to a capability:\n\n```\nUser: \"fix docker\"\n    │\n    ▼\nDetect: intent=fix, target=docker\n    │\n    ▼\nQuery capability registry for \"docker.repair\" or \"docker.diagnostic\"\n    │\n    ▼\nExecute via executor\n    │\n    ▼\nShow result\n```\n\n### 2.2 Fuzzy Matching\n\n| User says | Maps to |\n|-----------|---------|\n| `logs` | `ethan logs` |\n| `log api` | `ethan logs --service api` |\n| `status` | `ethan status` |\n| `state` | `ethan status` |\n| `help` | `ethan --help` |\n| `plugins` | `ethan plugin list` |\n\n---\n\n## 3. Proactive Suggestions\n\n### 3.1 Next Action Recommendations\n\nAfter completing a task, suggest related actions:\n\n```\n✓ Deployed to staging\n\n  What next?\n  → check staging health\n  → run tests\n  → deploy to production\n```\n\n### 3.2 Contextual Hints\n\n```\nUser: \"fix docker\"\nSuggestion: I can diagnose docker — run diagnostic?\n  → Yes, run docker.diagnostic\n  → No, just show status\n```\n\n### 3.3 Auto-Completion\n\nBased on history and context:\n```\nUser types: \"run tes\"\nSuggestion: Did you mean?\n  → run pytest\n  → run tests\n```\n\n---\n\n## 4. Prompt Intelligence API\n\n```python\nclass PromptIntelligence:\n    @staticmethod\n    def classify(input: str) -> PromptIntent:\n        \"\"\"Return intent type + extracted params.\"\"\"\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def suggest(input: str, history: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n        \"\"\"Return suggested actions.\"\"\"\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def next_actions(last_intent: PromptIntent) -> list[str]:\n        \"\"\"Recommend follow-up actions.\"\"\"\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def execute(intent: PromptIntent) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Execute intent if unambiguous.\"\"\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. Interaction Flows\n\n### 5.1 Direct Execution\n\n```\nUser: \"fix docker\"\n    │\n    ▼\nConfidence: high (exact match to known pattern)\n    │\n    ▼\nExecute: ethan run docker.diagnostic\n    │\n    ▼\nShow result: ✓ Docker is healthy\n```\n\n### 5.2 Confirmation Prompt\n\n```\nUser: \"deploy staging\"\n    │\n    ▼\nConfidence: medium (ambiguous)\n    │\n    ▼\nConfirm: Deploy what to staging?\n  → Deploy current project\n  → Deploy service <name>\n  → Cancel\n```\n\n### 5.3 Clarification\n\n```\nUser: \"fix\"\n    │\n    ▼\nConfidence: low (missing target)\n    │\n    ▼\nPrompt: Fix what?\n  → docker\n  → api\n  → database\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. Capability Mapping\n\nKnown intent → capability mapping:\n\n| Intent | Capability | Fallback |\n|--------|------------|----------|\n| `fix <target>` | `<target>.diagnostic` → `<target>.repair` | Show status |\n| `check <target>` | `<target>.health` | Show info |\n| `deploy <target>` | `<target>.deploy` | confirm |\n| `run <cmd>` | `shell.run` | direct exec |\n| `logs [for X]` | `logs.tail` | show hint |\n| `status` | `system.state` | direct query |\n| `help` | (built-in) | show help |\n\n---\n\n## 7. Confidence Levels\n\n| Level | Behavior |\n|-------|----------|\n| **High** (≥0.9) | Execute directly, show result |\n| **Medium** (0.6–0.9) | Show suggestion, wait for confirm |\n| **Low** (<0.6) | Ask for clarification |\n\n---\n\n## 8. Example Session\n\n```\n◆  ethan  ◇  idle  ▸ fix docker\n\n  ◆  ethan  ◇  thinking  ▸\n  ■  Detected intent: fix docker\n  ■  Querying docker.diagnostic capability...\n  ✓  Docker is healthy (0.8s)\n\n  What next?\n  → check docker stats\n  → deploy app\n  → run tests\n\n◆  ethan  ◇  idle  ▸ _\n```","operationIsLocatedInWorkspace":true,"startLineNumbers":[]}

{"tool":"newFileCreated","path":"cli/core/intent.py","content":"\"\"\"ETHAN Prompt Intelligence — intent detection, smart suggestions, auto-execution.\n\nUsage:\n    from core.intent import PromptIntelligence\n\n    pi = PromptIntelligence()\n    intent = pi.classify(\"fix docker\")\n    if intent.confidence >= 0.9:\n        pi.execute(intent)\n    else:\n        pi.suggest(intent)\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\n\n# Command registry for smart_cmd detection\nKNOWN_COMMANDS = [\"chat\", \"run\", \"status\", \"logs\", \"plugin\", \"shell\", \"help\", \"daemon\", \"config\"]\n\n# Intent patterns: (regex, intent_type, extractor)\nINTENT_PATTERNS = [\n    (r\"^(fix|repair|debug)\\s+(\\w+)$\", \"fix\", lambda m: {\"target\": m.group(2)}),\n    (r\"^(check|health|diagnose)\\s+(\\w+)(?:\\s+(\\w+))?$\", \"check\", lambda m: {\"target\": m.group(2), \"aspect\": m.group(3) or \"\"}),\n    (r\"^(run|execute|exec)\\s+(.+)$\", \"run\", lambda m: {\"cmd\": m.group(2)}),\n    (r\"^(deploy)\\s+(\\w+)(?:\\s+to\\s+(\\w+))?$\", \"deploy\", lambda m: {\"target\": m.group(2), \"env\": m.group(3) or \"\"}),\n    (r\"^(logs|log)\\s*(?:for\\s+(\\w+))?$\", \"logs\", lambda m: {\"service\": m.group(2) or \"\"}),\n    (r\"^(status|state|info)$\", \"status\", lambda m: {}),\n    (r\"^(help|--help|-h)$\", \"help\", lambda m: {}),\n]\n\n# Fuzzy command map (shorthand → full command)\nFUZZY_MAP = {\n    \"logs\": \"logs\",\n    \"log\": \"logs\",\n    \"status\": \"status\",\n    \"state\": \"status\",\n    \"info\": \"status\",\n    \"help\": \"help\",\n    \"plugins\": \"plugin list\",\n    \"plugin\": \"plugin list\",\n    \"chat\": \"chat\",\n    \"run\": \"run\",\n}\n\n\nclass PromptIntent:\n    \"\"\"Detected user intent with confidence and params.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: str, confidence: float, params: dict, raw: str):\n        self.kind = kind  # command, intent, chat, smart_cmd\n        self.confidence = confidence\n        self.params = params\n        self.raw = raw\n\n    def __repr__(self):\n        return f\"PromptIntent({self.kind}, {self.confidence:.2f}, {self.params})\"\n\n\nclass PromptIntelligence:\n    \"\"\"Detect and act on user intent from natural input.\"\"\"\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def classify(text: str) -> PromptIntent:\n        text = text.strip()\n        if not text:\n            return PromptIntent(\"chat\", 0.0, {}, text)\n\n        # 1. Exact command match\n        first = text.split()[0]\n        if first in KNOWN_COMMANDS:\n            return PromptIntent(\"command\", 1.0, {\"cmd\": text}, text)\n\n        # 2. Smart command (shorthand)\n        if first in FUZZY_MAP:\n            return PromptIntent(\"smart_cmd\", 0.95, {\"cmd\": FUZZY_MAP[first], \"args\": text[len(first):].strip()}, text)\n\n        # 3. Intent patterns\n        for pattern, kind, extractor in INTENT_PATTERNS:\n            m = re.match(pattern, text, re.IGNORECASE)\n            if m:\n                return PromptIntent(\"intent\", 0.9, extractor(m), text)\n\n        # 4. Default: chat\n        return PromptIntent(\"chat\", 0.0, {\"text\": text}, text)\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def suggest_next(history: list[str], current: PromptIntent) -> list[str]:\n        \"\"\"Suggest next actions based on history and current intent.\"\"\"\n        suggestions = []\n        if current.kind == \"intent\":\n            if current.params.get(\"target\") == \"docker\":\n                suggestions = [\"check docker stats\", \"deploy app\", \"run tests\"]\n            elif current.params.get(\"target\") == \"api\":\n                suggestions = [\"check api health\", \"run api tests\", \"restart api\"]\n            else:\n                suggestions = [\"run tests\", \"check status\", \"show logs\"]\n        elif current.kind == \"smart_cmd\" and current.params.get(\"cmd\") == \"logs\":\n            suggestions = [\"logs --follow\", \"status\", \"run tests\"]\n        elif current.kind == \"status\":\n            suggestions = [\"run tests\", \"deploy staging\", \"show logs\"]\n        return suggestions[:3]\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def autocomplete(prefix: str, history: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n        \"\"\"Suggest completions for a partial input.\"\"\"\n        prefix = prefix.lower()\n        # From fuzzy map\n        matches = [v for k, v in FUZZY_MAP.items() if v.startswith(prefix)]\n        # From history\n        hist = [h for h in history if h.lower().startswith(prefix)]\n        # Merge, deduplicate, limit\n        seen = set()\n        result = []\n        for m in matches + hist:\n            if m not in seen:\n                seen.add(m)\n                result.append(m)\n            if len(result) >= 5:\n                break\n        return result\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def confidence_label(conf: float) -> str:\n        if conf >= 0.9:\n            return \"high\"\n        if conf >= 0.6:\n            return \"medium\"\n        return \"low\"","operationIsLocatedInWorkspace":true,"startLineNumbers":[]}

{"tool":"newFileCreated","path":"OUTPUT_FORMATTING.md","content":"# ETHAN Output Formatting System\n\n## Philosophy\n\nOutput is communication, not decoration. Every character must serve a purpose. Readable, structured, minimal noise. Terminal-safe first.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Foundations\n\n### 1.1 Design Principles\n\n| Principle | Rule |\n|-----------|------|\n| **Terminal-safe** | No 24-bit color, no background fills, no Unicode combining |\n| **Scannable** | Headers, bullets, spacing make structure obvious at a glance |\n| **Consistent** | Same concepts always look the same |\n| **Minimal** | Remove decorative elements; keep only functional whitespace |\n| **Resilient** | Degrade gracefully on width < 80 columns |\n\n### 1.2 Anatomy of an Output Block\n\n```\n┌─ Header ─────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│ ◆  Section Title                                  │\n│                                                   │\n│   ✓  success line                                 │\n│   →  list item                                    │\n│       code example here                           │\n│                                                   │\n│ ─ footer ──────────────────────────────────────── │\n│   ⏱ 2.3s                                          │\n└───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n---\n\n## 2. Headers\n\n### 2.1 Section Header\n\n```python\ndef section(title: str, subtitle: str = \"\") -> str:\n    return f\"{C.BLUE}{I.SECTION} {title}{C.RESET}  {C.DIM}{subtitle}{C.RESET}\"\n```\n\n```\n◆ Result    [POST /v1/message 201]\n```\n\n### 2.2 Sub-header\n\n```python\ndef subheader(text: str) -> str:\n    return f\"{C.BOLD}{text}{C.RESET}\"\n```\n\n```\nProperties\n```\n\n### 2.3 Divider\n\n```python\nDIVIDER = f\"{C.DIM}{'─' * 40}{C.RESET}\"\n```\n\n```\n─────────────────────────────────────────────\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. Success / Warning / Error States\n\n### 3.1 Success (green)\n\n```\n✓  Deployed 3 services\n```\n\n```python\ndef success(msg: str) -> str:\n    return f\"  {C.GREEN}{I.CHECK} {msg}{C.RESET}\"\n```\n\n### 3.2 Warning (yellow)\n\n```\n⚠  Disk space low (12% free)\n```\n\n```python\ndef warning(msg: str) -> str:\n    return f\"  {C.YELLOW}{I.WARN} {msg}{C.RESET}\"\n```\n\n### 3.3 Error (red, structured)\n\n```\n✗ Connection refused\n  → host: localhost:4222\n  → try: ethan daemon start\n```\n\n```python\ndef error(title: str, context: str = \"\", suggestion: str = \"\") -> str:\n    parts = [f\"  {C.RED}{I.CROSS} {title}{C.RESET}\"]\n    if context:\n        parts.append(f\"    {C.DIM}{I.ARROW} {context}{C.RESET}\")\n    if suggestion:\n        parts.append(f\"    {C.CYAN}{I.ARROW} {suggestion}{C.RESET}\")\n    return \"\\n\".join(parts)\n```\n\n### 3.4 Info (cyan)\n\n```\nℹ  Running diagnostics...\n```\n\n```python\ndef info(msg: str) -> str:\n    return f\"  {C.CYAN}{I.INFO} {msg}{C.RESET}\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## 4. Code Blocks\n\n### 4.1 Inline Code\n\n```\nUse `docker build` to create an image.\n```\n\n```python\ndef inline_code(text: str) -> str:\n    return f\"{C.CYAN}`{text}`{C.RESET}\"\n```\n\n### 4.2 Fenced Code Block (terminal-safe)\n\n````\n    ┌─ Python ─────────────────────────────────┐\n    │ def hello():                             │\n    │     print(\"Hello, World!\")               │\n    └──────────────────────────────────────────┘\n````\n\n```python\ndef code_block(language: str, code: str) -> str:\n    lines = code.strip().split(\"\\n\")\n    header = f\"{C.DIM}┌─ {language} {'─' * max(0, 40 - len(language))}┐{C.RESET}\"\n    footer = f\"{C.DIM}└{'─' * 40}┘{C.RESET}\"\n    body = \"\\n\".join(f\"    {C.WHITE}{line}{C.RESET}\" for line in lines)\n    return f\"{header}\\n{body}\\n{footer}\"\n```\n\n**Rules**:\n- Max width 42 chars (inner content)\n- Language label in header\n- 4-space outer indent\n- No syntax highlighting (Just White on Dim border)\n- Truncate lines > 40 with `…`\n\n### 4.3 Multi-line Output\n\n```\n  output line 1\n  output line 2\n  output line 3\n```\n\n```python\ndef output_lines(lines: list[str]) -> str:\n    return \"\\n\".join(f\"  {C.DIM}{line}{C.RESET}\" for line in lines)\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. Tables (terminal-safe)\n\n### 5.1 Simple Table\n\n```\n  Name           Status    Port\n  ─────────────────────────────\n  api-gateway   ● ONLINE  8080\n  user-service  ● ONLINE  3000\n  db            ○ OFFLINE -\n```\n\n```python\ndef table(headers: list[str], rows: list[list[str]], status_col: int = -1) -> str:\n    col_widths = [max(len(str(h)), max((len(str(r[i])) for r in rows), default=0)) for i, h in enumerate(headers)]\n    # Header\n    out = [f\"  {'  '.join(h.ljust(w) for h, w in zip(headers, col_widths))}\"]\n    # Divider\n    out.append(f\"  {'  '.join('─' * w for w in col_widths)}\")\n    # Rows\n    for row in rows:\n        cells = []\n        for i, cell in enumerate(row):\n            cell = str(cell)\n            if i == status_col:\n                # Status column: preserve Unicode icons\n                cells.append(cell.ljust(col_widths[i]))\n            else:\n                cells.append(cell.ljust(col_widths[i]))\n        out.append(f\"  {'  '.join(cells)}\")\n    return \"\\n\".join(out)\n```\n\n### 5.2 Status Icons in Tables\n\n| Icon | Meaning | Color |\n|------|---------|-------|\n| `● ONLINE` | Running, healthy | Green |\n| `○ OFFLINE` | Stopped | Dim |\n| `◐ DEGRADED` | Partial failure | Yellow |\n| `✗ ERROR` | Crashed | Red |\n\n### 5.3 Table Rules\n\n- Column separator: 2 spaces\n- Header divider: `─` repeated per column width\n- No vertical borders (too noisy)\n- Max 6 columns (beyond that: use `key: value` pairs instead)\n- Truncate cells > max_width with `…`\n\n---\n\n## 6. Lists\n\n### 6.1 Unordered List\n\n```\n  → first item\n  → second item\n    with continuation\n  → third item\n```\n\n### 6.2 Numbered List\n\n```\n  1.  first step\n  2.  second step\n  3.  third step\n```\n\n```python\ndef numbered_list(items: list[str], start: int = 1) -> str:\n    width = len(str(len(items) + start))\n    return \"\\n\".join(\n        f\"  {str(i).rjust(width)}.  {item}\" for i, item in enumerate(items, start=start)\n    )\n```\n\n### 6.3 Definition List (key: value)\n\n```\n  name:      my-service\n  version:   1.2.0\n  status:    ● ONLINE\n```\n\n```python\ndef definition_list(pairs: dict[str, str]) -> str:\n    max_key = max(len(k) for k in pairs) if pairs else 0\n    return \"\\n\".join(\n        f\"  {k.ljust(max_key)}:  {v}\" for k, v in pairs.items()\n    )\n```\n\n---\n\n## 7. Metadata & Timing\n\n### 7.1 Timing Footer\n\n```\n  ⏱ 2.3s\n  @ 2026-06-23T20:00:00Z\n```\n\n```python\ndef timing(duration: float, timestamp: str = \"\") -> str:\n    parts = [f\"{C.DIM}{I.TIMER} {duration:.1f}s{C.RESET}\"]\n    if timestamp:\n        parts.append(f\"{C.DIM}@ {timestamp}{C.RESET}\")\n    return f\"  {'  '.join(parts)}\"\n```\n\n### 7.2 Counters\n\n```\n  3 services  |  2 warnings  |  0 errors\n```\n\n```python\ndef counters(**kwargs: int) -> str:\n    parts = [f\"{v} {k}\" for k, v in kwargs.items()]\n    return f\"  {C.DIM}{'  |  '.join(parts)}{C.RESET}\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## 8. Spinner & Progress\n\n### 8.1 Animated Spinner\n\n```\n  ◐ Loading...\n```\n\nRotates through `◐◓◑◒`. Use `Streamer` from `core/streaming.py`.\n\n### 8.2 Progress Bar\n\n```\n  [████████░░░░]  67%  (3/5 plugins installed)\n```\n\n```python\ndef progress(current: int, total: int, width: int = 12, label: str = \"\") -> str:\n    filled = int(width * current / total) if total > 0 else 0\n    bar = \"█\" * filled + \"░\" * (width - filled)\n    pct = int(100 * current / total) if total > 0 else 0\n    suffix = f\"  {pct}%\"\n    if label:\n        suffix += f\"  ({label})\"\n    return f\"  [{C.CYAN}{bar}{C.RESET}]{suffix}\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## 9. Combining Blocks\n\n### 9.1 Full Example\n\n```python\nprint()\nprint(section(\"Deploy Result\", \"POST /v1/deploy\"))\nprint()\nprint(success(\"Deployed 3 services\"))\nprint(warning(\"API health check pending\"))\nprint(error(\"DB connection slow\", \"latency 1.2s\", \"check network\"))\nprint()\nprint(subheader(\"Services\"))\nprint(table(\n    [\"Name\", \"Status\", \"Port\"],\n    [\n        [\"api-gateway\", \"● ONLINE\", \"8080\"],\n        [\"user-service\", \"● ONLINE\", \"3000\"],\n        [\"db\", \"○ OFFLINE\", \"-\"],\n    ],\n    status_col=1\n))\nprint()\nprint(timing(2.3, \"2026-06-23T20:00:00Z\"))\nprint(counters(services=3, warnings=2, errors=0))\nprint()\nprint(code_block(\"bash\", \"ethan logs --follow\"))\nprint(divider())\n```\n\n### 9.2 Block Spacing\n\n- 1 blank line before a section\n- 0 blank lines inside a section (between elements)\n- 1 blank line after a section\n- 4-space indent for nested content\n\n---\n\n## 10. Graceful Degradation\n\n| Condition | Adaptation |\n|-----------|-------------|\n| Width < 80 | Wrap long cells, reduce progress bar to 8 chars |\n| No color support | Strip ANSI, show `[OK]` instead of `✓` |\n| No Unicode | Replace `─◆●○✗⚠` with ASCII `-*ox!` |\n| Piped output | Remove spinner/animation, keep structure |\n\n```python\ndef section(title, subtitle=\"\"):\n    if not sys.stdout.isatty():\n        return f\"[SECTION] {title}\"\n    return f\"{C.BLUE}{I.SECTION}{C.RESET} {title}\"\n```","operationIsLocatedInWorkspace":true,"startLineNumbers":[]}

{k.ljust(max_key)}:  {v}\" for k, v in pairs.items()\n    )\n\n\ndef timing(duration: float, timestamp: str = \"\") -> str:\n    \"\"\"Timing footer.\"\"\"\n    parts = [f\"{C.DIM}{I.TIMER} {duration:.1f}s{C.RESET}\"]\n    if timestamp:\n        parts.append(f\"{C.DIM}@ {timestamp}{C.RESET}\")\n    return f\"  {'  '.join(parts)}\"\n\n\ndef counters(**kwargs: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Counter footer.\"\"\"\n    parts = [f\"{v} {k}\" for k, v in kwargs.items()]\n    return f\"  {C.DIM}{'  |  '.join(parts)}{C.RESET}\"\n\n\ndef progress(current: int, total: int, width: int = 12, label: str = \"\") -> str:\n    \"\"\"Progress bar.\"\"\"\n    filled = int(width * current / total) if total > 0 else 0\n    bar = \"█\" * filled + \"░\" * (width - filled)\n    pct = int(100 * current / total) if total > 0 else 0\n    suffix = f\"  {pct}%\"\n    if label:\n        suffix += f\"  ({label})\"\n    return f\"  [{C.CYAN}{bar}{C.RESET}]{suffix}\"","operationIsLocatedInWorkspace":true,"startLineNumbers":[]}
